title: On-Chip Endothelial Inflammatory Phenotyping
protocol: Cut 3-inch circular substrates from a 100 x 20 mm tissue culture dish using a lathe.
Sterilize substrates by submersion in 70% ethanol.
Place sterilized substrates in a Petri dish and coat with 4 ml type-I collagen (100 μg/ml) for 1 hr at room temperature.
Rinse coated substrates with 4 ml of 1 x PBS.
Suspend Human Aortic Endothelial Cells (HAEC, passage 4-6) at 6.5x10^5 cells/ml.
Seed the suspended HAEC by applying 1 ml directly to each substrate.
Place seeded substrates in a 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator and allow cells to adhere for 1 hr.
Add 9 ml of Endothelial Growth Medium-2 (EGM-2) supplemented with 1x antibiotic-antimycotic solution to the adhered cells.
Change media every 2 days until cells reach 90% confluency.
Maintain THP-1 cells in RPMI 1640 medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 1x antibiotic-antimycotic solution.
Passage THP-1 cells when they reach a density of 10^6 cells/ml.
Prepare the custom cone-and-plate Cell Shearing Device (CSD).
Sterilize the chamber housing with ethanol.
Rinse the sterilized chamber housing with sterile PBS.
Heat the chamber housing to 37 °C.
Level the chamber housing to ensure the cone is perpendicular to the cell monolayer.
Assemble the substrate with the cells into the bottom of the housing.
Set the cone to the desired height.
Use Leibovitz-15 (L-15) medium supplemented with Endothelial BulletKit as the shearing medium.
Add tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α, 0.5 ng/ml) to the shearing medium.
Inject 6 ml of the TNF-α-containing medium into the device via a syringe connected to an inlet port, avoiding air bubbles in the chamber.
Shear cells at high magnitude steady shear stress (HSS, 15 dyne/cm2).
Shear cells at oscillatory shear stress (OSS, 0 ± 5 dyne/cm2, 1 Hz) for 4 hours.
Adjust cone alignment with the substrate to within 0.05° through precision leveling.
Set gap height at 20 ± 10 μm using a depth gauge.
Remove cells from the device after shearing.
Prepare cells for analysis of monocyte adhesion.
Obtain master mold for desired microfluidic channel number and channel height.
Design network of channels using CAD software (Autodesk Inventor).
Print design at 5000 dpi on transparency.
Spin negative photoresist (SU8) onto a silicon wafer to a thickness of 100 μm.
Overlay transparency on photoresist and expose to UV light.
Remove non-polymerized photoresist to generate positive replica master.
Mix silicone base with silicone curing agent at a ratio of 10:1 by weight in a weigh boat.
Stir PDMS solution with a 5 ml serological pipet, being careful not to add plastic flakes.
Pour the PDMS solution into a Petri dish containing the master wafer.
Cover the Petri dish and place it into a vacuum container for 15 minutes.
Remove excess bubbles by gently blowing air over the surface after vacuum treatment.
Place the Petri dish in an oven at 70 °C for 1 hour.
Cut out microfluidic chambers using a sharp blade.
Turn on light source to inverted microscope.
Set heater to 37 °C.
Attach tubing to a 10 ml syringe and fill with distilled water to eliminate bubbles.
Place the syringe in the syringe pump.
Set flow rate to induce a wall shear stress of 1 dyne/cm2.
Use a 100 μl micropipette to remove air from the individual channels.
Attach vacuum adapter to PDMS chamber.
Ensure that the valve on the vacuum adapter is set to off.
Place Petri dish with HAEC monolayer over the objective.
Place PDMS chamber over the Petri dish and carefully set it on the HAEC monolayer while assuring that no air bubbles form between the device and the monolayer.
Turn the valve so that the vacuum is on and the chamber is firmly attached.
Cut 19 gauge needles blunt such that there is only 5 mm of metal left.
Fill the plastic reservoir with buffer and put into PDMS chamber entrance.
Attach tubing from syringe pumps to PDMS channel exits.
Suspend THP-1 cells at 2x10^6 cells/ml in HBSS + Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ + 0.1% HSA.
Incubate THP-1 cells with stromal derived factor-1 (SDF-1, 50 μg/ml) for 15 min at room temperature to activate the cells.
Turn on syringe pump to establish flow, then add 50 μl of cell suspension to reservoir without introducing air bubbles.
Once flow is fully developed, begin data acquisition.
Run for 5 min at appropriate flow rate, adding buffer to the reservoir if the solution gets low.
Continue flowing buffer into the channels to wash out any unbound cells in the flow stream.
Acquire digital image sequences at 3 frames/s for 2 min following fully developed flow along the longitudinal axis of the channel at 3 locations in the channel.
Count the number of arrested cells per field.
Identify their phase-bright appearance in the same focal plane as the monolayer.
Define firm cell arrest by movement < ½ cell diameter in 10 s.
Average data over 3 random fields / channel.
Quantify using ImageJ software.
